items.summary:

It discusses how some of these patterns may become lasting elements in software design while others remain specific to AI contexts.

Examples include the sparkle emoji becoming associated with AI, the contrast between AI app icons and native system icons, and UI behaviors influenced by AI's non-deterministic nature. The author reflects on how these emerging aesthetics might spread and influence software interaction paradigms for years to come.

Anthropic halted all cyber evaluations upon discovery, notified affected parties, and is collaborating with its evaluation partner Irregular to investigate and remediate the issues. The affected models lacked standard safeguards but operated on isolated infrastructure separate from Anthropic's sensitive systems.

The committee expects the policy to evolve and plans to review it periodically.

items.title: Researchers distill Chinese DeepSeek model into GPT-OSS without transferring political censorship, improving financial reasoning performance [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Show HN: Distilling DeepSeek into GPT-OSS doesn't transfer censorship. Try it
items.summary:
Researchers investigated whether political censorship from a Chinese AI model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, transfers when distilled into an American model, GPT-OSS-120B. They found that while the distilled model improved financial reasoning, it did not inherit the teacher's censorship on China-sensitive topics, responding openly to questions about sensitive issues like Xinjiang labor programs.

The study involved 152 matched prompt pairs scored by four independent judges, showing DeepSeek's selective censorship on Chinese topics but no significant censorship in the distilled model. The researchers published their evaluation tools, data, and models to support transparency and further research on distillation effects and censorship transfer in AI models.

That’s 9 percentage points faster than it reported for the March quarter, and more than double the growth rate for the same period last year. 

Just as strikingly, AWS’ operating profit margin also rose, to 39.4%, the highest since the start of last year. To lift its operating margin while grappling with rising depreciation expenses on new chips and servers is an accomplishment. Amazon stock jumped 9% in response, suggesting investors were more focused on AWS’ accelerating growth than on the huge capital investments it is making to drive future growth. As a reminder of the size of those investments, Amazon burned $7.6 billion in cash in the quarter and raised its 2026 capital expenditures projection by $20 billion to $220 billion.

items.summary:
Graphics processing units are all the rage, but startups developing the networking equipment that connects GPUs to one other are getting some love from investors, too. The latest is Xsight, a nine-year-old startup based in Israel that makes server networking and storage chips, the latter of which are also in high demand in the current boom.

Five years after its last major fundraising, Xsight has raised $300 million at a $2.8 billion valuation, the company told The Information exclusively. The fundraising round was led by Fidelity Investments, the mutual fund giant. Gavin Baker’s Atreides Management, a longtime AI hardware investor and former Fidelity portfolio manager, as well as Valor Equity Partners, Battery Ventures and Intel Capital also participated. 

The deal follows fundraising in the past month by networking startups Eliyan and Upscale AI, which notched $1 billion and $2 billion valuations, respectively.
